Remembers the server and page you had open. Starts the local server first if it isn\'t running.
Keep screen on while the local server runs
Only while CoCode is in the foreground. Leaving the app lets the screen sleep normally.
Installs a small Linux system on this phone and runs T3 Code or OpenChamber with your coding agents inside it. Your projects and sessions stay on the device.
Alpine Linux, Node.js, Git, the servers you pick and agent CLIs
About 1.2 GB to download and store
Takes a few minutes and keeps going in the background
That may not be enough space.
You can leave the app. Setup keeps going in the background and shows its progress in a notification.
%1$s is installed. Start the server to open it.
Repair reinstalls the Linux system. Your projects are kept when possible.
Running a server on the device needs an ARM64 (arm64-v8a) or x86_64 phone or tablet. You can still connect to a T3 Code or OpenChamber server on your computer below.
Choose at least one agent CLI to install. The servers find them on PATH.
Select at least one coding agent.
Checking an agent installs it next to the ones you have. Unchecking an installed agent and tapping Apply uninstalls it.

Only the agents you unchecked are uninstalled; adding an agent never removes another. Their settings and sign-ins in the home folder and your projects are kept, so you can check them again later. The local server restarts if it is running.
T3 Code is unavailable until the update is done. You can leave the app. The update keeps going in the background and shows its progress in a notification.

T3 Code stops during the update and starts again afterwards, so running tasks are interrupted. The update downloads up to a few hundred MB and takes several minutes. Projects and settings are kept, and if anything fails, the current version keeps working.
The update downloads up to a few hundred MB and takes several minutes. T3 Code can\'t start until it\'s done. Projects and settings are kept, and if anything fails, the current version keeps working.
The current version is still installed and works as before.

Keep projects and the OpenCode, Codex and Claude Code folders in CoCode/ on your phone\'s storage, so you can open them with a file manager or over USB. The Codex and Claude Code folders are shared in full, including sign-ins and session history.
CoCode needs all-files access to use this folder. You can turn it on in system settings.
CoCode needs access to your phone\'s storage to use this folder.
Other apps with all-files access can read this folder.
Other apps with storage access can read this folder.
All of Codex, including the sign-in (auth.json) and sessions
All of Claude Code, including the sign-in (.credentials.json) and sessions
Codex and Claude Code sign-ins and session history are in this folder. File managers and other apps with storage access can read them and use your accounts.
Kept inside the app: ~/projects-private, ~/.claude.json, OpenCode sessions (~/.local/share/opencode), OpenCode\'s service password and node_modules.
Share the agent folders, including sign-ins?
These folders on your phone\'s storage become the real folders the agents use:

The Codex and Claude Code folders are shared in full: their login credentials (auth.json, .credentials.json), sessions and history are stored there. File managers and other apps with storage access can read them, copy them and use your accounts.
Your current settings and sign-ins are copied there once; nothing inside the app is deleted. Turning this off later doesn\'t copy changes back.
I understand that other apps can read my sign-ins and sessions
Turning this on puts the Codex and Claude Code sign-ins and session history in this folder. File managers and other apps with storage access can then read them and use your accounts.
Codex and Claude Code aren\'t shared yet

This folder was turned on in an earlier version, so only projects/ and opencode/ are shared. This version can also share the full Codex and Claude Code folders, including their sign-ins and sessions. Nothing changes until you agree.
Kept inside the app: ~/.codex, ~/.claude, ~/projects-private, ~/.claude.json, OpenCode sessions (~/.local/share/opencode), OpenCode\'s service password and node_modules.
Your files stay in CoCode/ on your phone\'s storage; nothing there is deleted or copied back. From the next server start, projects and OpenCode settings come from the app again.
CoCode has access, but can\'t create CoCode/ on your phone\'s storage. Make sure the storage is available.
Shared storage doesn\'t keep symlinks or executable bits — use ~/projects-private for projects that need node_modules.

Everything stays in CoCode/ on your phone\'s storage; nothing there is deleted or copied back. From the next server start, Codex and Claude Code use the copies inside the app again. Those are from before you turned this on, so they may be out of date: you may need to sign in again, and newer sessions and settings are only in CoCode/.
This stops the local server, deletes the Linux system and installs it again with the servers and agents you picked, which downloads about 1.2 GB. Your projects are kept when possible.
This stops the local server and deletes the Linux system from this phone, including both servers, projects, sessions and settings stored inside it. Saved servers are not affected.

This stops the local server and deletes the Linux system from this phone, including everything stored inside it. The CoCode/ folder on your phone\'s storage is kept, including the Codex and Claude Code sign-ins and sessions in it. Saved servers are not affected.
Add the address of a T3 Code or OpenChamber server on your computer or network, for example 192.0.2.20:3773.

A newer version of CoCode has been released. Download the APK from the release page and install it over this one; your servers, projects and settings are kept.
Pick one or both. Only one runs at a time; both use the same home folder and OpenCode settings.
Checking a server installs it next to the other one. Unchecking an installed server and tapping Apply uninstalls only that server.
%1$s stops and %2$s starts in its place, so tasks running in %1$s are interrupted. Projects, the home folder and OpenCode settings are shared and stay as they are.
%2$s is used from now on. %1$s stays installed, and projects, the home folder and OpenCode settings are shared.
Only the unchecked server is uninstalled. The other server, your projects, the home folder and the OpenCode, Codex and Claude Code settings are kept. The local server restarts if it is running.
Pick what runs at this address, so CoCode signs in the right way.
